scope: Release-mode CPU state work after dense input; simulated clock gaps, not GPU rendering, physical suspend or desktop latency.
limits: Two runs on a shared host without CPU affinity or frequency isolation; timings are observations, not worst-case bounds or predictions for other hardware.
First run may overlap owned native rendering; repeat runs before the compositor rebuild and hardware GPU measurement.
Reachable dense input retains 154 events after coalescing and retention; the separate 256-entry case restores older events only to stress capacity.
Two to four second gaps still replay the recent bounded integration interval; no runtime optimization or default change accompanies this measurement.
This benchmark isolates one motion state and excludes GPU drawing, uploads, allocation outside the state and presentation.

first.capacity_stress: Restores all 256 chronological entries of the same input trace, including entries production retention discarded; no state, target or event cadence changes. This is not a reachable steady-state input history.
first.scope: CPU-only state advance; no renderer, presentation, physical suspend or real-time latency claim
